summary: With the last minutes I closed the account with a protection direction that follows directly from the traced mechanism rather than from any new claim: the state exists because the configuration scan starts after the replayed committed prefix (api.go 611-613), so scanning configuration entries from the snapshot index onward — instead of from max(lastSnapshot, lastApplied)+1 — would keep the committed entries applied to the FSM while still rebuilding the configuration from the log; and since the failure is silent, a start-time comparison between the reconstructed configuration and the newest configuration entry the node's own log or snapshot carries (refusing to serve, or at least reporting, when a voter's configuration is empty or older than that entry) would surface the state where indexes alone cannot, because the log is complete and the commit and applied indexes look healthy. That sits alongside the earlier detection note and its false-positive caution. The record now ends complete: one root cause with an execution-confirmed trigger and causal refinement, four consequence classes with controls and repeats, the safety violation including the loss of an acknowledged client command, the progress losses with their operator remediation, the client-contract consequence, the four repair paths with reachability boundaries, negative results, a hash-verified harness set, recorded knowledge uses, an audited citation set, no open gaps, and two honest notes about an over-broad claim I corrected and a merge artifact I could not repair.
